answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can transact, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking a thousand means locking a thousand stakes, and a lone agent in the tundra of new accounts still has to earn trust through countersigned work before it can move real value. A jade ledger of verified history makes that work visible, and an attacker hitting its nadir loses the stake, not just the account, so creating fresh identities stops paying off.
